description: This case study is the synthesis report of the independent analysis, commissioned by the Walloon government, of how waterways and dams were managed during the storms of 12 July 2021 that flooded the Vesdre valley in Belgium. It sets out the lot 2 recommendations built on the lot 1 findings. The lot 1 conclusions summarised in it say the event was rare to very rare, with Vesdre flows above the 100-year flood and nearly twice the highest recorded rainfall, a two-peak flood on 14 to 15 July, and bridge blockages that worsened flooding. The Eupen dam clipped the flood peak and its operation followed the dam manual, though the speed of the flood prevented pre-releases and the manual does not allow them. Findings on management include no legal framework for dam control, no external review of dams run by the regional public service, a critical basin configuration, no legal ban on building in flood zones, non-binding flood plans, weak flood alarms and crisis organisation. Recommendations are coded by domain, for example BAR for dams, PRE for prevention, PLA for planning and crisis management, and SUP for extras. Coverage: one river basin, one event, in French. Access: free PDF; licence not stated. Caveats: this record rests on the synthesis report, not the full lot 1 report. It informs dam operation, flood warning and crisis response scenarios, and relates to the Vesdre 2021 population distribution data record in the catalogue.
